pthm-rpm-inverse-momentum-and-work.physical_scope: Conditional kinematic identities for a massive point particle of constant positive mass in one inertial chart of flat Minkowski spacetime, plus a separate variable-mass ansatz; no force law or variable-mass dynamics is adopted.

pthm-rpm-inverse-momentum-and-work:
## Statement

Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, and let $x:I\to A$ be a $C^2$ future-timelike worldline in the flat Minkowski model of [[def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline]]. Use one inertial frame and parameterize the curve by that chart's time coordinate $t$, so its coordinates are $(ct,\mathbf x(t))$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]). Identify the observer rest space with $\mathbb R^3$ by the frame's spatial orthonormal basis and use its Euclidean dot product and norm ([[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]). Write $\mathbf v=d\mathbf x/dt$, $\gamma=(1-|\mathbf v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, proper time $\tau$, and $U=dx/d\tau$. In the constant-mass sector of [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]], let $m>0$ be constant and $P=mU$. In this chart write $P=(E/c,\mathbf p)$, where $E$ and $\mathbf p$ are the observer energy and spatial momentum of [[def-rpm-mechanical-momentum-and-observer-energy]]. Then $|\mathbf v|<c$, $E=\gamma mc^2>0$, $\mathbf p=\gamma m\mathbf v$, and

$$E^2=m^2c^4+c^2|\mathbf p|^2,\qquad \mathbf v=\frac{c^2\mathbf p}{E}.$$

Define the three-force by $\mathbf F:=d\mathbf p/dt$ and the four-force by $K:=dP/d\tau$ in this flat inertial chart. In SI units $m$ is in kilograms, $c$ and $\mathbf v$ in metres per second, $E$ in joules, $\mathbf p$ in kilogram metres per second, and $\mathbf F,K$ in newtons. Then

$$\frac{dE}{dt}=\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf v,\qquad K=\gamma\left(\frac{\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf v}{c},\mathbf F\right).$$

Separately, let $I_\tau\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open proper-time interval, let $m:I_\tau\to(0,\infty)$ be $C^1$, and let $U:I_\tau\to V$ be a $C^1$ future timelike vector field with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$. Measure $m$ in kilograms and $dm/d\tau$ in kilograms per second, and set $P(\tau):=m(\tau)U(\tau)$. With $K:=dP/d\tau$, the kinematic ansatz satisfies

$$\eta(P,K)=-m\,\frac{dm}{d\tau}\,c^2.$$

The last identity is only a differentiated mass-shell relation; it prescribes no evolution for $m$. None of these conclusions assumes a force law.
thm-rpm-finite-future-momentum-sum:
## Statement

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model with $c>0$, and fix an inertial frame. For a finite nonempty list $P_1,\ldots,P_N$ of nonzero future-causal vectors in $V$, let $Q:=\sum_{i=1}^N P_i$, let $m_i:=\sqrt{-\eta(P_i,P_i)}/c$ (so $m_i=0$ exactly for a null leg), and let $M(Q)$ be the invariant mass of the total when $Q$ is timelike, as defined in [[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]].

Then $Q$ is nonzero and future causal. If at least one $P_i$ is timelike, then $Q$ is future timelike. If all $P_i$ are null, then $Q$ is null exactly when all $P_i$ lie on the same future null ray; otherwise $Q$ is future timelike. Whenever $Q$ is timelike, the center-of-momentum frame exists, its time-axis observer $n_Q=Q/(M(Q)c)$ has zero total spatial momentum and total observer energy $M(Q)c^2$, and

$$M(Q)\ge\sum_{i=1}^N m_i.$$

Equality holds exactly when every $P_i$ is massive and there is one future unit timelike vector $n$ such that $P_i=m_i c\,n$ for every $i$. A nonzero future-null total has no center-of-momentum frame.

def-rpm-collision-objects.physical_scope: Finite event-local collision data for classical point particles and ideal null legs in the adopted flat relativistic-particle model; no interaction law, collision occurrence, probability, or curved-spacetime total-energy claim.

def-rpm-collision-objects:
## Definition

Use the flat oriented, time-oriented affine Minkowski model, signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and SI convention $x^0=ct$ of [[def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline]]. A **relativistic-particle-mechanics collision configuration** is a mass-specified causal collision datum of [[def-sr-collision-datum-and-conservation]]: an event $p\in A$, a finite nonempty incoming list $P_1,\ldots,P_N\in V$, and a finite nonempty outgoing list $P'_1,\ldots,P'_K\in V$, where every leg is a nonzero future-causal vector in the same displacement space $V$. A massive leg has a recorded mass $m>0$ and the massive-sector momentum of [[def-rpm-mechanical-momentum-and-observer-energy]]; a null leg has recorded mass $0$ and is a nonzero future-null vector with its scale specified independently. The definition does not identify a null momentum with $mU$ at $m=0$.

The side totals are the finite vector sums $Q_{\rm in}:=\sum_{i=1}^N P_i$ and $Q_{\rm out}:=\sum_{j=1}^K P'_j$. All legs are attached to the same event, so the sums compare vectors in one affine displacement space; no transport between different events is part of the datum. The adjective **isolated** is reserved for a model condition used by the postulate below: no external four-momentum transfer during the idealized event and no omitted incoming or outgoing leg.

At an event, an **observer** is a future unit timelike vector $n$ with $\eta(n,n)=-1$, and its rest space is $n^\perp=\{v\in V:\eta(v,n)=0\}$, as in [[def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline]]. Observer energy $E_n(P):=-c\eta(P,n)$ and spatial momentum $q_n(P):=P+\eta(P,n)n\in n^\perp$ are those of [[def-rpm-mechanical-momentum-and-observer-energy]]. Their units are joules and kilogram metres per second. An inertial laboratory means one named inertial chart and its time-axis observer; it is not a general observer congruence or an arbitrary coordinate chart.

post-rpm-isolated-collision-balance.physical_scope: Scoped reuse in relativistic-particle mechanics of the existing special-relativity isolated-collision postulate, for finite complete event data in flat Minkowski spacetime; no collision occurrence, mechanism, probability, or rate is asserted.

post-rpm-isolated-collision-balance:
## Postulate

For the relativistic-particle-mechanics collision configurations of [[def-rpm-collision-objects]], adopt the isolated-collision balance already stated in clause (iii) of [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]: when the event is isolated and the incoming and outgoing lists contain every leg, $Q_{\rm in}=Q_{\rm out}$. This local postulate records the exact collision interface used on this page; it is a scoped reuse of the existing adopted model assumption, not a second independent conservation assumption.

The balance is an adopted physical premise. It does not show that any specified reaction occurs and supplies no interaction mechanism, selection rule, probability, cross section, or amplitude. The cited treatments motivate and explain the model formulation; they do not turn the postulate into a deductive theorem or a report of an observed collision.

pthm-rpm-system-mass-threshold.physical_scope: Necessary kinematic rest-mass thresholds for a finite, complete, isolated event in flat relativistic-particle mechanics; no interaction probability, coupling, selection rule, or claim that a channel occurs.

pthm-rpm-system-mass-threshold:
## Statement

Let a mass-specified isolated collision configuration of [[def-rpm-collision-objects]] satisfy the balance postulate [[post-rpm-isolated-collision-balance]]. Write its common total as $Q:=Q_{\rm in}=Q_{\rm out}$. It is nonzero future causal, and it is timelike if either side contains a massive leg. If $Q$ is future timelike, let $M:=\sqrt{-\eta(Q,Q)}/c$, and let $\mu_{\rm in}$ and $\mu_{\rm out}$ be the sums of the recorded rest masses on the two sides. Then

$$M\ge\mu_{\rm in},\qquad M\ge\mu_{\rm out}.$$

In particular, a proposed final collection with total rest mass $\mu$ requires the invariant squared energy $\sigma:=-c^2\eta(Q,Q)=M^2c^4$ to satisfy $\sigma\ge\mu^2c^4$. If an actual final collection contains a nonzero null leg, then the inequality is strict. Equality is kinematically attained exactly when every leg on the relevant side is massive and all its four-momenta are proportional to the same future unit timelike vector. This is a necessary kinematic condition; it does not establish that the interaction realizes the channel.

If instead $Q$ is future null, each side consists only of null legs on one common future null ray; no center-of-momentum frame exists and no positive-mass final leg is compatible with that total. In SI units $m_i,M,\mu$ are kilograms, $Mc^2$ is joules, and $\sigma$ is joules squared.

pthm-rpm-fixed-target-threshold.physical_scope: Necessary invariant-energy threshold for a massive projectile incident on a massive target at rest in one named inertial laboratory frame; it is a kinematic condition and does not predict a reaction rate or occurrence.

pthm-rpm-fixed-target-threshold:
## Statement

In a named inertial laboratory frame, let a massive projectile of rest mass $m_1>0$ and energy $E_1$ strike a massive target of rest mass $m_2>0$ initially at rest. Let the incoming momenta be $P_1=(E_1/c,\mathbf p_1)$ and $P_2=(m_2c,\mathbf 0)$, and let $\mu\ge0$ be the sum of the rest masses in a proposed final state of a finite isolated collision. Then

$$\sigma:=-c^2\eta(P_1+P_2,P_1+P_2)=m_1^2c^4+m_2^2c^4+2m_2c^2E_1.$$

The necessary final-state threshold from [[pthm-rpm-system-mass-threshold]] is $\sigma\ge\mu^2c^4$, hence

$$E_1\ge\frac{(\mu^2-m_1^2-m_2^2)c^2}{2m_2},\qquad E_1\ge m_1c^2.$$

If a nonzero null final leg is required, the invariant-mass inequality is strict, $\sigma>\mu^2c^4$; the displayed invariant threshold can then be an unattained endpoint. These are kinematic necessities, not guarantees of a physical channel.

In SI units $m_1,m_2,\mu$ are kilograms, $E_1$ is joules, and $\sigma$ is joules squared.

pthm-rpm-two-body-com-kinematics.physical_scope: Exact two-product momentum-balance kinematics in the center-of-momentum frame of a timelike total in flat relativistic-particle mechanics; no interaction probability, cross section, or claim that a channel occurs.

pthm-rpm-two-body-com-kinematics:
## Statement

Let a finite isolated collision have future-timelike total $Q$ of invariant mass $M>0$, and set $W:=Mc^2$. Suppose the complete outgoing list consists of exactly two legs, with recorded rest masses $a,b\ge0$; by the adopted balance postulate, their four-momenta must sum to $Q$. In a center-of-momentum frame with time-axis observer $n_Q$, a nonzero two-product state with $\mathbf p_a+\mathbf p_b=0$ exists exactly when

$$W\ge(a+b)c^2\quad\hbox{if }a,b>0,\qquad W>(a+b)c^2\quad\hbox{if }a=0\hbox{ or }b=0.$$

When it exists, there are $k\ge0$ and a unit vector $\mathbf e\in n_Q^\perp$ such that $\mathbf p_a=k\mathbf e$ and $\mathbf p_b=-k\mathbf e$. The energies and momentum magnitude are

$$E_a=\frac{W^2+(a^2-b^2)c^4}{2W},\qquad E_b=\frac{W^2+(b^2-a^2)c^4}{2W},\qquad k^2=\frac{[W^2-(a+b)^2c^4][W^2-(a-b)^2c^4]}{4W^2c^2}.$$

For $a,b>0$ at threshold, $k=0$ and the direction is immaterial. If a massless product is present, the strict threshold is required because a zero momentum would be the forbidden zero four-vector. These equations describe kinematic balance only. In SI units $a,b,M$ are kilograms, $W,E_a,E_b$ are joules, and $k$ is kilogram metres per second; the norm and dot product on $n_Q^\perp$ are induced by $\eta$.

pthm-rpm-two-null-invariant-energy.physical_scope: Invariant energy of two nonzero future-null incoming momenta as resolved in one named inertial laboratory observer; no collision outcome or reaction channel is asserted.

pthm-rpm-two-null-invariant-energy:
## Statement

Let $P_1,P_2$ be two nonzero future-null incoming momenta in a finite collision configuration, and let $n$ be the future unit observer of a named inertial laboratory frame. Define $E_i:=E_n(P_i)>0$, $\mathbf p_i:=q_n(P_i)$, and equip $n^\perp$ with the induced Euclidean inner product $\langle u,v\rangle_n:=\eta(u,v)$ and norm $|u|_n:=\sqrt{\langle u,u\rangle_n}$. Let $\theta\in[0,\pi]$ be their spatial angle, $\cos\theta=\langle\mathbf p_1,\mathbf p_2\rangle_n/(|\mathbf p_1|_n|\mathbf p_2|_n)$. For $Q:=P_1+P_2$ and $\sigma:=-c^2\eta(Q,Q)$,

$$\sigma=2E_1E_2(1-\cos\theta),\qquad M(Q)=\frac{\sqrt{\sigma}}{c^2}.$$

The total $Q$ is null exactly when $\theta=0$ (the two incoming vectors lie on one future null ray); it is timelike for $\theta>0$. In particular, for head-on momenta $\theta=\pi$, $M(Q)=2\sqrt{E_1E_2}/c^2$; if $E_1=E_2=E$, this is $2E/c^2$. The angle and the two energies depend on the named observer, while $\sigma$ and $M(Q)$ are invariant.

In SI units $E_1,E_2$ are joules, $\sigma$ is joules squared, and $M(Q)$ is kilograms; $\theta$ is dimensionless.

pthm-rpm-kinematic-elastic-channel.physical_scope: Kinematic freedom of the outgoing direction for a two-product elastic channel with fixed masses and timelike total in flat relativistic-particle mechanics; no scattering law, angular distribution, or interaction rate is inferred.

pthm-rpm-kinematic-elastic-channel:
## Statement

Consider a two-product elastic channel in a finite isolated collision: the complete incoming and outgoing lists each have exactly two legs, their recorded rest masses agree pairwise, the total four-momentum is timelike, and the balance postulate is adopted. In the center-of-momentum frame, let the incoming momenta be $k\mathbf e_{\rm in}$ and $-k\mathbf e_{\rm in}$ in the spatial rest space $n_Q^\perp$, where $k\ge0$ is fixed by [[pthm-rpm-two-body-com-kinematics]]. Every admissible outgoing pair has the same momentum magnitude $k$. If $k>0$, any unit vector $\mathbf e_{\rm out}\in n_Q^\perp$ gives an on-shell outgoing pair $k\mathbf e_{\rm out},-k\mathbf e_{\rm out}$ with the same total four-momentum; thus kinematics alone leaves the full direction sphere available. If $k=0$, both products are at rest and the direction is undefined. No isotropic or uniform distribution of directions follows.

texp-rpm-ideal-fusion-mass.physical_scope: Hypothetical flat-spacetime event of two equal-mass classical particles forming one product with no other leg, conditional on the isolated-balance postulate; no actual reaction, interaction mechanism, probability, or empirical observation is asserted.

texp-rpm-ideal-fusion-mass:
## Statement

In a hypothetical isolated event, let two massive particles of equal rest mass $m>0$ have opposite velocities $\mathbf v$ and $-\mathbf v$ in one inertial laboratory, with $|\mathbf v|<c$ and $\gamma=(1-|\mathbf v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$. Suppose, as a stipulated possible channel, that they form one massive product at rest in that laboratory and that there are no other incoming or outgoing legs. Conditional on the balance postulate, the product rest mass is

$$M=2m\gamma,$$

so its excess rest mass over the two incoming rest masses is $2m(\gamma-1)$, and the corresponding rest-energy increase is $2m(\gamma-1)c^2$. This equals the incoming kinetic energy in the specified laboratory. When $\mathbf v=0$, the excess is zero. The item does not assert that such a perfectly complete fusion channel occurs in nature.

texp-rpm-one-null-decay-recoil.physical_scope: Hypothetical two-product decay in the classical massive-plus-null test-particle sectors, conditional on finite isolated momentum balance; no decay probability, quantum photon-energy relation, or empirical claim is asserted.

texp-rpm-one-null-decay-recoil:
## Statement

Hypothetically, a parent of rest mass $M>0$ is initially at rest and undergoes an isolated event into one massive daughter of rest mass $m$ and one nonzero future-null leg, where $0<m<M$; there are no other legs or external transfers. Under the balance postulate, in the parent rest frame the daughter and null momenta are opposite with common magnitude

$$k=\frac{(M^2-m^2)c}{2M}>0.$$

Their energies and the daughter speed are

$$E_{\rm null}=\frac{(M^2-m^2)c^2}{2M},\qquad E_{\rm d}=\frac{(M^2+m^2)c^2}{2M},\qquad |\mathbf v_{\rm d}|=\frac{(M^2-m^2)c}{M^2+m^2}<c.$$

The null-leg energy is strictly less than the full rest-energy difference $(M-m)c^2$; the remainder is the daughter's kinetic energy $(M-m)^2c^2/(2M)$. This is a conditional classical kinematic construction, not an assertion about a decay channel in nature.
